title: Transient Quota Slices + Ephemeral Boost Tokens — Billing Reconciler and Autoscale Hooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a controlled burst mechanism that lets Dedicated customers consume temporary additional throughput without permanent capacity changes, paired with a billing reconciliation system to surface and charge for overage usage. This ticket covers: the transient quota slice (TQS) abstraction in the control plane, ephemeral boost tokens in the runtime scheduler, autoscaler policy extensions for controlled decay and refill, and the billing reconciler that aggregates minute-level overages into customer invoices with grace credit handling. The solution must preserve latency SLOs, avoid noisy neighbor effects inside a dedicated fleet, and provide clear Console visibility for customers and SREs.
acceptance_criteria: - TQS API implemented in control plane and documented in the API spec; - Runtime accepts ephemeral boost tokens and enforces per-pool burst_factor + decay; - Autoscaler respects burst_headroom and does not immediately scale down until grace window expires; - Billing reconciler produces per-customer overage report and integrates with invoicing pipeline; - No regression in median P99 latency under synthetic burst tests; - Console shows burst consumption, estimated overage charges, and links to reconcile; - End-to-end integration tests and canary rollout plan signed off by Product and Finance.
design_notes: Design summary: introduce a TQS object attached to a Dedicated pool (fields: capacity_snapshot, burst_budget, refill_policy, decay_seconds). The runtime uses short-lived ephemeral boost tokens minted by control-plane when customer requests or policy triggers (API or Console). Tokens carry a consumption budget (in token-seconds / effective-GPU-seconds) and an expiration timestamp. Autoscaler policy extension 'burst_aware' will consider burst_budget when deciding scale-down, using a configurable hold_time and decay curve to prevent oscillation.
implementation_plan: 1) Control plane: TQS schema + API endpoints + quota accounting service (ENG-8532-CP). 2) Runtime: token ingestion, enforcement, and metrics emission (ENG-8532-RT). 3) Autoscaler: extend policy evaluator to read TQS and burst flags (ENG-8532-AS). 4) Billing: aggregator that consumes minute-granularity usage (from metrics pipeline), computes overage, applies grace credits, writes to billing queue. 5) Console: new panel surface and warnings. 6) Feature flag gating and canary rollout across 3 regions.
testing_plan: Unit tests for control plane accounting logic; fuzz tests for token minting/revocation; end-to-end scenario tests simulating a spike that consumes ephemeral boost then falls back; chaos tests for preemption and token loss; performance benchmarks verifying no >1% overhead for steady-state requests. Add synthetic load tests replicating customer traffic (see load profiles in links).
rollout_plan: - Stage 1: internal dogfood on dev clusters with feature flag (2 weeks). - Stage 2: limited customer beta for 3 tenants (assign early adopters) with billing reconciliation in dry-run mode (no charges) for 2 weeks. - Stage 3: enable billing for beta tenants with opt-in. - Stage 4: GA with gradual ramp and monitoring alerts for overage spikes and reconciler failures. Rollback plan: revoke token issuance and drain active tokens; autoscaler defaults to legacy policy.
